summary: Prešov Air Base is a Slovak Air Force military installation located near the city of Prešov in eastern Slovakia. It serves as an operational base primarily for rotary-wing aircraft and has historically hosted fighter units, including MiG-29s that were eventually transferred to Ukraine in 2023. The base also supports occasional NATO exercises and allied operations in the region.
faqs:
Q: Is Prešov Air Base open to civilian passengers?
A: No, this is a military airfield operated by the Slovak Air Force and is not available for regular commercial or civilian passenger flights.

Q: What aircraft are based at Prešov?
A: The base primarily hosts military helicopters supporting Slovak Armed Forces operations, following the retirement and transfer of its former MiG-29 fleet.

Q: Can pilots land at Prešov with permission?
A: Prior permission from the Slovak military authorities is required, and PPR requests must be coordinated well in advance through official channels.

Q: What is the nearest civilian airport to Prešov?
A: Košice International Airport (KSC) is the closest major civilian airport, located roughly 40 km south of the air base.
transport_tips: The base is located a few kilometers north of Prešov city center, best reached by car via road routes from the E50 highway. Public transport options are limited; taxi or pre-arranged military transport is the most reliable way to access the facility. Košice International Airport is the nearest commercial gateway for civilian travelers visiting the region.
local_tip: If you happen to be in Prešov for an authorized visit, take a short drive into the historic city center to see the iconic Saint Nicholas Concathedral, one of the oldest Gothic churches in Slovakia with striking interior frescoes.
